newsitem.title: CANADA: Canfor says Nielssen resigns as CEO.
newsitem.headline: Canfor says Nielssen resigns as CEO.

text.p: Canfor Corp announced on Friday the surprise resignation of President and Chief Executive Arild Nielssen.
The forestry company gave no reason for his departure and said he would be replaced on an interim basis by Chairman Peter Bentley. Nielssen also resigned as a director.
Bentley, 67, is a former Canfor chief executive, a major shareholder and a member of one of Canfor's founding families.

Nielssen replaced Bentley at the helm of Canfor little more than two years ago. He had risen through the ranks at Canfor and was described at the time of his appointment as part of a long-term succession plan.
Canfor officials were not immediately available for further comment, but analysts were caught off guard by the news.
"That surprises me," said one analyst. Nielssen "was always sort of low profile. Peter Bentley has always had a much higher profile. I guess they may have had a falling out."
Nielssen's departure cames a day after Canfor reported a jump in second-quarter earnings to C$15.6 million versus a loss of C$12.7 million a year ago.
In a brief telephone interview, Nielssen declined to discuss the reasons for his departure, saying he would have to give the matter more thought before commenting.
Another analyst who declined to be identified said there had been a rift between Nielssen and Bentley over Canfor's strategic direction.
"Bentley has run the company for years with a strong hand. I think if somebody disagrees with him, that's it," he said.
Canfor stock was down 0.05 at 14.50 in Toronto.
The company said it would search for a suitable replacement for Nielssen.

There has long been speculation that Bentley's daughter, Barbara Hislop, who holds the position of group vice president for coastal operations, was destined for a larger role in the company. Family members control about 40 percent of Canfor's stock.
